Hi Sarah / Marissa —

Following up with the technical fitment details you requested. I'll keep this concise and put numbers at the top; downstream notes explain assumptions.

Assumptions:
- Model family: mix of open Llama-3 style 70B quantized and a smaller 13B embedding model for vector ingest.
- Sequence length: 2048 tokens for generation; embedding jobs average 512 tokens.
- QoS target: 99th pct tail latency target for interactive lane = 120ms; batch embedding can tolerate higher latency (1–2s).

Recommended GPU mix (pilot -> base -> scale):
- Pilot (month 0–3): 4 x H100-type nodes (low-latency lane) + 8 x A100-40-type nodes (batch/throughput lane)
- Base (month 4–9): 12 x H100 + 16 x A100-40 (balanced)
- Scale (month 10–12+): add burst pool of 8 mixed GPUs (on-demand reserved burst)

Per-GPU throughput (tokens/sec, single request stream assumptions, KV cache warm):
- H100 (generation, 2048 ctx): 650–780 tokens/sec (steady-state, 1-stream per GPU)
- A100-40 (generation quantized path): 420–520 tokens/sec
- A100-40 (embedding workload, 512 ctx): 4,000–5,500 embeddings/sec (small-batch optimized)

Tail-latency & batching guidance:
- Keep interactive lane batch-window <= 5ms and prioritize single-stream scheduling; use pre-warmed KV cache and pinned model instances for H100 lane.
- For embedding fleet, use larger batch windows (50–200ms) with dynamic batching to maximize token density.
- Suggest a tiny hot-pool (2 nodes) pinned for extremely short spike handling to keep 99.9th below 200ms during burst periods.

Kernel/quantization fit notes:
- For the 70B family, we recommend fp16 kernels where possible; when using 4-bit QAT quant profiles expect a 10–15% throughput advantage but plan for additional validation on hallucination/regression risk.
- Kernel selection: switch to fused attention kernels for generation >1024 seq; fallback to generic kernels for short sequences to reduce overhead.

Commitment phasing proposal (pricing + operational):
- Pilot: 3-month reserve at 30% of projected base commit, includes onboarding credits and two optimization sessions.
- Base: 9-month commit at target throughput with monthly throughput reconciliation and a quarterly quality gate.
- Burst: separate burst entitlement that can be consumed and trued-up monthly.

Attachments: I've uploaded a quick fitment matrix with per-GPU numbers and suggested slotting (gpu-fitment-matrix.csv).

If helpful, I can run a short perf test on your sanitized model weights next week and return measured token/sec numbers.

Cheers,

Sarah / Ops team —

Quick answers inline and a proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) to keep procurement on schedule.

1) Pilot with A100-only (no H100 warm lane):
- Expected perf: 20–30% lower peak tokens/sec for generation vs H100; steady-state latency (99th) likely to rise to ~180–240ms at 2K seq under similar load.
- Cost delta: A100-only pilot reduces pilot-capex by ~18% vs mixed pilot; however the ops cost to maintain tighter batch windows increases marginally. We included a conservative scenario in the workbook showing pricing impact.

2) Operational guardrails for rollout/regression detection:
- Quality gate: require benchmark evals on a fixed prompt suite and holdback comparison (baseline vs canary) with threshold for log-prob divergence and hallucination rate.
- Automated rollback: 5-minute canary window with automatic rollback triggers on >5% regression on critical prompts or >2x error rates.
- Audit artifacts: maintain per-deployment eval snapshots, token-level sampling logs (retention policy configurable), and a weekly QA digest for auditors.

3) Holiday peak planning (Dec 20–Jan 5):
- For a 2x planned peak QPS we recommend pre-booking a 1.2–1.5x burst pool (not full 2x) because dynamic autoscaling plus warm KV cache handles residual demand. For OpsAI's target profile that maps to ~6–10 additional mixed GPUs for the pilot/base windows.

Mutual Action Plan (high level):
- Dec 15: Sign pilot SOW & exchange sanitized model artifacts (DocuSign link below).
- Dec 18–22: Redwood runs pilot perf tests on sanitized weights (2 days).
- Jan 4: Pilot review — throughput, tail-latency, quality gate results.
- Jan 15: Finalize base commit sizing and pricing for 9-month term.
